get.description:
The signed-in account, for a client that has a token and wants the rest.

A token carries an id and an admin flag and deliberately nothing else, so a page that
needs the cook's name or chosen language asks for it rather than reading it out of a
credential.
Everything this cook owns, in the portable format (FR-11).

post.description: Read an exported document into this instance (UC-1.2).

parameters.name: servings

schema.description: Show the recipe at this yield, in whatever the recipe itself yields.
schema.title: Servings

parameters.description: Show the recipe at this yield, in whatever the recipe itself yields.

post.description:
Read a recipe off a web page (UC-1.3).

Every failure here is reported with what a cook can do about it. "It did not work" is
a bug report; "this site will not serve an automated reader, but the page works in
your browser" is an interface.

get.description: Find registry entries to point a recipe line, or a dietary constraint, at.
How many people, and how many servings that comes to.

put.description:
Rewrite an eater, constraints included.

A whole-person replacement rather than a patch, so removing a constraint in the form
removes it here — there is no shape of request that leaves a deleted allergy behind.

get.description: What is still missing from this cook's setup, and what comes next.

post.description:
Answer a setup question outright — "nobody has any", "the defaults are fine".

The one stored part of setup. Without it a household where nobody has a dietary
restriction is indistinguishable from one nobody has been asked about, and setup
would go on asking forever (FR-15).

put.description: Remember the language this cook reads in, wherever they sign in from.

get.description: Every kind of ingredient, and the unit this cook reads it in.

put.description: Choose the unit for one kind of ingredient.

AgeBand.title: AgeBand
AgeBand.description:
Drives *suitability* — honey for infants, texture, portion appropriateness.

Deliberately separate from appetite: two adults of the same age eat different amounts,
and folding the two together would mean misjudging either portions or safety.

Allergen.title: Allergen
Allergen.description:
The allergen classes that must be declared on food sold in the EU and Switzerland.

A fixed, externally defined list rather than free text: a constraint and an ingredient
have to mean the same thing by "nuts" for a verdict to be worth anything. Anything
outside these fourteen is avoided by ingredient instead.

Authenticated.title: Authenticated
Authenticated.description: A signed-in cook and the token proving it.

BootstrapState.title: BootstrapState
BootstrapState.description: Whether the instance still needs its first admin.

ConstraintView.title: ConstraintView
ConstraintView.description:
One thing an eater avoids, as a client reads and writes it.

The same shape in both directions, so an interface can read a household, edit it, and
send it back without translating between two nearly-identical types.

Cook.title: Cook
Cook.description:
A cook account, safe to pass anywhere in the application.

The password hash is deliberately absent. Anything needing it asks for a
`StoredCredential`, which keeps credentials on the authentication path instead of
riding along in every value that happens to describe a cook.

Credentials.title: Credentials
Credentials.description: A request to sign in. No length rule — an old password is still the password.

EaterInput.title: EaterInput
EaterInput.description:
An eater being recorded or corrected (UC-6.3, UC-6.4, UC-6.5).

Carries the whole person, constraints included, because that is what an editing form
holds. A partial update would need a way to say "and remove this allergy", and the
version that forgets to is the one that quietly keeps it.

EaterView.title: EaterView
EaterView.description:
Somebody at the table, as a client reads them.

`appetite` is a string for the same reason a quantity's magnitude is: JSON numbers
are binary floats in a browser, and these are summed to decide how much food to cook.

ExchangeDocument.title: ExchangeDocument
ExchangeDocument.description: A portable set of recipes and the registry entries they use.

ExchangeIngredient.title: ExchangeIngredient
ExchangeIngredient.description: Enough to recreate a registry entry on an instance that lacks it.

FindingView.title: FindingView
FindingView.description: One reason behind a verdict, as a client reads it.

HouseholdSummary.title: HouseholdSummary
HouseholdSummary.description:
How many people are cooked for, and how much food that is.

Two different numbers on purpose: four people is not four servings once anybody eats
more or less than a standard portion (FR-18). Computed by `MeasureEngine` rather than
in the browser, so planning, shopping, and this screen cannot come to disagree.

ImportedRecipe.title: ImportedRecipe
ImportedRecipe.description:
What importing a page did, as well as what it produced.

`ingredients_added` is the part a cook has to act on: names the registry had never
seen are recorded so the recipe can exist, and nothing is known about their allergens
until somebody looks. Reporting them is what stops that being a silent addition.

IngredientKind.title: IngredientKind
IngredientKind.description:
What sort of thing this is, for the purpose of measuring it.

This is the axis a cook's unit preferences run along: powders in grams, liquids in
millilitres (UC-6.2). It is deliberately coarse — it exists to choose a unit, not to
classify food.

IngredientLineInput.title: IngredientLineInput
IngredientLineInput.description: One line of a recipe being authored.

IngredientView.title: IngredientView
IngredientView.description: A registry entry as a client reads it.

LocaleChoice.title: LocaleChoice
LocaleChoice.description: The language a cook reads in.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description: The answer, worst-first when several apply.

PresentedRecipe.title: PresentedRecipe
PresentedRecipe.description: A recipe scaled and rendered for one cook, ready to display.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description:
How a recipe came to exist (V1).

Recorded because it is worth knowing, but a recipe's usefulness never depends on it —
every path ends in the same canonical structure.

QuantityView.title: QuantityView
QuantityView.description:
A quantity as a client reads it.

`magnitude` is a string. JSON numbers are binary floats in a browser, and 0.1 of a
gram is not worth losing to that; `display` is what a screen actually shows.

Registration.title: Registration
Registration.description:
A request to create an account.

The password rule lives here rather than in the manager: it constrains the shape of
the input, so it is the contract's business, and stating it here means the API
rejects a short password before any work is done.

SetupProgressView.title: SetupProgressView
SetupProgressView.description: What is still missing from the setup, and what to do next (UC-10.3).

SetupStep.title: SetupStep
SetupStep.description:
The things worth establishing, in the order they are worth asking for.

Who is eating comes first because it is what the product is about; everything after it
is a preference about how the answer is shown.

Severity.title: Severity
Severity.description:
How seriously a constraint is meant, which is what decides behaviour.

Without this every constraint is treated alike, and either a disliked ingredient bars a
menu or a life-threatening allergen appears as a suggestion. Both are wrong.

Source.title: Source
Source.description:
Where a reading came from, which is worth keeping.

A recipe that came out wrong is a different investigation depending on whether the
page lied in its metadata or a model misread its prose.

UnitChoice.title: UnitChoice
UnitChoice.description: The unit a cook wants this kind of ingredient shown in.

UnitPreferenceView.title: UnitPreferenceView
UnitPreferenceView.description:
One kind of ingredient and the unit this cook reads it in.

`chosen` separates a preference from a default. Everybody has defaults, and having
them is not an answer — which is what lets guided setup tell the two apart (FR-15).

UrlImport.title: UrlImport
UrlImport.description: A page to read a recipe out of (UC-1.3).

VerdictView.title: VerdictView
VerdictView.description:
Whether the household can eat this, and why.

Absent rather than `suitable` when there is nobody to judge against: a reassurance
about a question nobody asked is worse than silence, and a cook who has not yet
described their household should be told nothing rather than told yes.

Visibility.title: Visibility
Visibility.description: Private by default; publishing is explicit (FR-5).
